title: Retardation in a quartz plate at 633 nm
caption: The two polarisations pick up a phase difference Δφ = 2π(n_e − n_o)d/λ. With n_e − n_o = 0.0092 at 633 nm it grows by 5.23° per μm of quartz, so a quarter-wave plate (90°, linear ↔ circular) is d = λ/4Δn = 17.2 μm thick, and a half-wave plate (180°) twice that.
alt: Graph of retardation in degrees against plate thickness in micrometres: a straight line through the origin reaching 90 degrees at 17.2 micrometres and 180 degrees at 34.4 micrometres.
description: The horizontal axis is the plate thickness in micrometres; the vertical axis is the phase difference between the two polarisations in degrees.
The line is Δφ = 360° × 0.0092 × d/0.633 μm = 5.23° per μm.
It reaches 90° (quarter-wave) at 17.2 μm and 180° (half-wave) at 34.4 μm.
